This Dashboard page presents the interactive visualization component of Homework 4 for P8105 Data Science. The dataset used is "the Instacart Online Grocery Shopping Dataset 2017". Detail information can be accessed [here](https://p8105.com/dataset_instacart.html). This analysis aims to explore the shopping behaviors of Instacart users. Click to go back [home](index.html). 


```{r, setup, include=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(flexdashboard)

# Load the Instacart dataset
data("instacart")
```



Row 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Shopping patterns across the week - Heatmap

```{r}
# How does the number of Instacart orders vary by day of the week and hour of the day? 
# Prepare data
instacart |> 
  distinct(order_id, order_dow, order_hour_of_day) |> 
  count(order_dow, order_hour_of_day, name = "n_orders") |> 
  group_by(order_dow) |> 
  mutate(
    percentage = 100 * n_orders / sum(n_orders), 
    day = factor(
      order_dow, 
      levels = 0:6, 
      labels = c("Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
                 "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday")
    )
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
# Create an interactive heatmap
  plot_ly(
    x = ~order_hour_of_day, 
    y = ~day, 
    z = ~n_orders, 
    customdata = ~percentage, 
    type = "heatmap", 
    colors = "Blues", 
    colorbar = list(title = "Number of orders"),
    xgap = 1.5, 
    ygap = 1.5, 
    hovertemplate = paste0(
      "Day: %{y}",
      "<br>Hour: %{x}:00",
      "<br>Number of orders: %{z}",
      "<br>Percentage of day's orders: %{customdata:.1f}%",
      "<extra></extra>"
    )
  ) |> 
  layout(
    title = "Number of Instacart orders by day of week and hour of day", 
    xaxis = list(title = "Hour of day"), 
    yaxis = list(title = "Day of week")
  )
```

> Instacard orders were concentrated during daytime hours, particularly between 9 AM and 5 PM, with relatively few orders overnight. Sunday showed the highest number of orders, especially around midday. Overall, shopping patterns were similar across the week despite the variation in order volums by day.

### Reordinging patterns by product department - Bar Chart

```{r}
# How do reorder rates vary across the 10 most frequently purchased product departments? 
# Prepare data for the top 10 frequently purchased product departments
instacart |>
  filter(!is.na(department), !is.na(reordered)) |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarize(
    total_items = n(),
    reordered_items = sum(reordered == 1),
    reorder_rate = round(100 * reordered_items / total_items, 1)
  ) |>
  slice_max(total_items, n = 10) |>
# Reorder departments by reorder rate
  mutate(
    department = fct_reorder(department, reorder_rate)
    ) |>
# Create an interactive bar chart
  plot_ly(
    x = ~reorder_rate,
    y = ~department, 
    type = "bar",
    color = ~department, 
    colors = "viridis", 
    customdata = ~total_items, 
    hovertemplate = paste0(
      "Department: %{y}",
      "<br>Reorder rate: %{x}%",
      "<br>Total items: %{customdata}",
      "<extra></extra>"
    )
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = "Reorder rates across top 10 product departments",
    xaxis = list(title = "Reorder rate (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Product department")
  )
```

> Reorder rates varied across product departments. The departments with highest reorder rates were dairy eggs, produce, and beverages, which all exceeded 65%. Pantry had the lowest reorder rate at approximately 36%. 



### Basket size across different times of day - Boxplot

```{r}
# How does the distribution of basket sizes vary across different times of day? 
# Prepare data
instacart |>
  count(order_id, order_hour_of_day, name = "basket_size") |>
  mutate(
    time_period = case_when(
      order_hour_of_day < 6 ~ "Night",
      order_hour_of_day < 12 ~ "Morning",
      order_hour_of_day < 18 ~ "Afternoon",
      TRUE ~ "Evening"
    ),
    time_period = factor(
      time_period,
      levels = c("Night", "Morning", "Afternoon", "Evening")
    )
  ) |>
# Create an interactive boxplot
  plot_ly(
    x = ~time_period,
    y = ~basket_size,
    color = ~time_period,
    type = "box",
    colors = "viridis", 
    boxpoints = "outliers"
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = "Distribution of basket sizes across different times of day",
    xaxis = list(title = "Time of day"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of products per order")
  )
```

> Basket size distributions were quite similar across the four time periods of the day. The median basket sizes for the four time periods were 9, and the interquartile ranges were also comparable. All groups showed right-skewed distributions, suggesting that most orders had relatively small basket sizes. But each time period also had many large order outliers.
